clue.text: See 21
Commander's not allowed in encore!

indicators.note: the word in is barred from the encore, so those letters are dropped from it

blocks.note: an encore is a performance given again
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frustrated performer is told the commander forbids any encore.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a military commander in the Ottoman Empire, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Aga was the title of an Ottoman officer or chief, so a commander.

clue.text: Thoroughly clean old Tudor building? Right to move away!

indicators.note: a building is something being put together, so the remaining letters are constructed afresh
the right is told to leave the Tudor, so that letter goes

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Spring-cleaning an old Tudor house, with someone told to get out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hides that building is the instruction to rearrange, not the Tudor house.
explanation.definitionFit: To do out a room is an informal British phrase for giving it a full, thorough cleaning.

clue.text: Typical example of Oriental religious book

blocks.note: E for East, the abbreviation crosswords use for Oriental
PI is the slangy short form of pious
a tome is a large, heavy book

explanation.surface: A sacred Eastern text held up as a model of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (short for pious) is a crossword staple for religious.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect specimen embodying the qualities of its class.

clue.text: Io's Guardian? And I — upset — left Guardian''s organisation

indicators.note: the letters of and I are knocked into a different order before being taken away
here the past tense of leave: the letters are left out, removed from the word
organising means arranging in order, so the leftover letters are set out anew

blocks.note: taken as written, the possessive s included
taken as written

explanation.surface: The newspaper's staff are in disarray after someone storms out of the office.
explanation.walkthrough: The second Guardian is the newspaper, and the letters of and I are scattered through it. Argus is also the name of several newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth hundred-eyed Argus was set by Hera to watch over Io, Zeus's lover turned into a heifer.

clue.text: Jockey, say, holding a small advantage

blocks.note: first meaning: a rider is the ... on a horse, as racecards say of a jockey
second meaning: a single point or move ahead of a rival

explanation.walkthrough: Racing reports name the rider with "up", so a jockey is the one who is up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a mounted rider and being narrowly ahead in a contest are both expressed by the same short phrase.

clue.text: How embarrassing, having to accommodate old writer's belly!

definitions.note: an archaic word for the belly, found only in old writers

indicators.note: the two opening words are made to house the answer inside them

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and the first two of the second

explanation.surface: Someone is mortified at having to make room for a fat old author's paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads as a reaction, but its words simply contain the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wem is an obsolete word for the womb or stomach, used by medieval authors such as Chaucer.

clue.text: Takes in Parisian living in student accommodation

indicators.note: the French word sits inside the lodgings

blocks.note: digs are rented lodgings, typical for students in Britain
EST is French for is, the verb of existing, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A French lodger living in a student house.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British slang for rented rooms; EST is French for is, existing or living.
explanation.definitionFit: To digest is to absorb food or information, the same as taking it in.

clue.text: See 21
See 21
Indiana's second step away from the pull of the earth?

definitions.text: away from the pull of the earth

blocks.note: IN is the postal abbreviation of the US state
S is the abbreviation for second
a pace is a single stride

explanation.surface: Indiana Jones taking a second step off the ground, as if escaping gravity.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer space lies beyond where Earth's gravity holds things down, so that is where weightlessness is found.

clue.text: See 21
Chess grandmaster cutting short both parts of unbelievable story

indicators.note: each half of the phrase loses its last letter, and both shortened halves come out the same

blocks.note: a tall story is one too far-fetched to believe

explanation.surface: A grandmaster dismisses an implausible yarn mid-sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The unbelievable story is a TALL TALE; cut short, both TALL and TALE leave the same three letters, which is the joke of both parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Tal was a Latvian world chess champion famed for daring attacks.

clue.text: Keeps making an endless pig's ear

indicators.note: the mess loses its final letter

blocks.note: making a pig's ear of something is British slang for botching it; a hash is the same kind of mess

explanation.surface: Someone keeps botching a job without ever finishing.
explanation.walkthrough: To make a pig's ear or a hash of something are both British idioms for making a mess of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something is to hold or retain it, as in keeping possession.

clue.text: See 21
Exhausted wrestlers may hold anything in this!

definitions.text: wrestlers may hold anything in this

blocks.note: first meaning: tired out, spent

blocks.clueFragment: wrestlers may hold anything in this
blocks.note: second meaning: a freestyle form of wrestling in which almost any hold is permitted

explanation.walkthrough: All-in wrestling is a style with few restrictions on holds.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is everyday British slang for worn out and also names an unrestricted wrestling style.

clue.text: A little drop of cold stuff — coke/lager getting upset

definitions.text: A little drop of cold stuff

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the beer upside down, reading it backwards

blocks.note: snow is slang for cocaine
Pils is a pale lager, short for Pilsner

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over a coke and a lager, spilling a few cold drops.
explanation.walkthrough: Coke here is the drug, not the drink; snow is its slang name.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowslip is a small avalanche, a modest fall of snow, so a little drop of cold stuff.

clue.text: See 21
A firm''s turned over in checks for birds

indicators.note: the company abbreviation is flipped to read backwards
the reversed firm is placed inside the word for checks

blocks.note: taken as written
to vet is to check thoroughly
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A company's accounts are flipped over during inspections.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocets are long-legged wading birds with upturned bills, emblem of the RSPB.

clue.text: Leader of party going after healthy Turkish dish

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so the word's opening letter is taken
the party's opening letter comes behind the word for healthy

blocks.note: hale means fit and strong, as in hale and hearty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party leader follows a healthy diet of Turkish food.
explanation.definitionFit: Halep is the Turkish name for Aleppo, which gives its name to Turkish kebab dishes cooked in the Aleppo style.

clue.text: See 16
Moving description of ponderous character from "Lear" given dazzling leading feature

annotation.answer: SLOWLY IT WANDERS PAUSES CREEPS ANON IT SPARKLES FLASHES AND LEAPS AND EVER AS ONWARD IT GLEAMING GOES A LIGHT ON THE BONG-TREE STEM IT THROWS

definitions.text: Moving description of ponderous character from "Lear" given dazzling leading feature

blocks.note: reads like praise for a touching passage, but means lines describing something in motion

blocks.clueFragment: ponderous character from "Lear" given dazzling leading feature
blocks.note: not King Lear but Edward Lear: a heavy-sounding creature whose foremost feature, its nose, shines

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around Lear point at the play, but the source is Edward Lear's nonsense poem The Dong with a Luminous Nose; a dong is the heavy toll of a bell, and the nose is the leading feature. The answer is the stanza tracing the light's path across the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: These lines from the poem trace the wandering glow of the creature's lit-up nose through the night, so they literally describe movement.

clue.text: Old church book-keeper, for the most part authoritative, sat around

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, all but its final letter
the word sat is placed around the shortened word, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written
crisp can describe a manner that is brisk and decisive, as in a crisp command

explanation.surface: A domineering old church clerk sits surrounded by the parish ledgers.
explanation.walkthrough: Book-keeper suggests an accountant, but this is the official who looked after a church's sacred books and vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrist, or sacristan, was the church officer in charge of the sacristy and its sacred vessels, vestments and service books.

clue.text: In dispute, it may be heard to require blessing single group of similar cells

linkWords: it may be heard to require blessing

blocks.note: A means one, a single thing
a tissue in biology is a mass of similar cells

explanation.surface: A biologist mid-argument sneezes and needs a hanky.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle part is an extra sound joke: said aloud the answer is atishoo, the sneeze that brings a blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the point being argued over, still contested.

clue.text: Homer's expression for money, say?

indicators.note: say signals the sound of a word, not its spelling

blocks.note: dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: A classicist wonders what the Greek poet called cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Homer is Homer Simpson, not the Greek poet.
explanation.definitionFit: D'oh is Homer Simpson's famous exasperated catchphrase.

clue.text: "She dances on the sand" in Brazil, nearly causing massive disturbance

definitions.text: "She dances on the sand" in Brazil

indicators.note: almost all of the word, its last letter dropped

blocks.note: a riot is a violent public disorder

explanation.surface: A beach dancer in Brazil almost starts a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted line is from Duran Duran's song Rio; Rio de Janeiro is also Brazil's famous beach city.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1982 hit's lyric runs: her name is Rio and she dances on the sand.

clue.text: See 21
Seductive singer inspires gorgeous Irene

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so these words hold the answer within them

blocks.note: the last letter of gorgeous and the first four of Irene run together

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman named Irene is the muse of an alluring vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sirens of Greek myth lured sailors to their deaths with enchanting song.

clue.text: See 21
Some living accommodation that provides reduction of note

blocks.note: first meaning: one apartment
second meaning: the musical note A lowered by a semitone

explanation.walkthrough: A flat sign lowers a note by a semitone, hence reduction.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a place to live, and the pitch a semitone below A is named the same way.

clue.text: What makes stray say "fish"?

blocks.note: the clue asks what turns the word stray into the word say: two of its letters taken out
the answer, split differently, is an instruction to remove those letters, and as one word it is a fish

explanation.walkthrough: Take TR out of STRAY and what is left is SAY; written as one word, TR OUT is a river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout are freshwater game fish of the salmon family, prized by anglers.

clue.text: See 21
In lead, top class drinking establishment

indicators.note: the class letter goes inside the chemical symbol

blocks.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
U means upper class, used of posh British manners

explanation.surface: A smart bar is the leader among upmarket venues.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub, short for public house, is a British bar serving drinks.

clue.text: See 21
The whole lot, or a fraction of it, did you say?

indicators.note: asks how the word is pronounced, pointing to a word sounding alike

blocks.note: some is part of a quantity

explanation.surface: A puzzled listener asks whether it was everything or only part.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the total and a part sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is the total amount, everything added together.
